items.title: Smooth cobordism triad for morse theory
items.statement: Work in ZFC. A compact smooth n-dimensional triad (W;M0,M1) has boundary the disjoint union of two closed faces with specified collars; either face may be empty. No orientability is required. In the oriented version the induced boundary orientation is (-M0) disjoint union M1. All manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable.
items.proof_plan: Fix boundary identifications and collars as data, including the empty manifold. Reverse the orientation of W when viewing an oriented cobordism backwards.
items.source_locator: Definition 1.3, printed p.2; local orientation convention from the published boundary definition

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Definition 1.3, printed p.2; local orientation convention from the published boundary definition

items.title: Morse function adapted to a cobordism
items.statement: An adapted Morse function f:W->[0,1] has f^{-1}(0)=M0, f^{-1}(1)=M1, only nondegenerate interior critical points, and in sufficiently small specified collars is t at M0 and 1-t at M1. Excellent means distinct interior critical values. Use a product metric when describing inward/outward gradients.
items.proof_plan: The collar clause makes the positive gradient inward on M0 and outward on M1. Downward fields have opposite signs.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Definition 2.3 p.8; Lemma 2.6 pp.9–10

items.title: Adapted excellent morse functions exist on compact cobordisms
items.statement: Every compact smooth triad admits an adapted excellent Morse function, with its prescribed linear boundary germs retained.
items.proof_plan: Patch linear boundary functions and the interior constant 1/2. Apply relative density on the boundaryless interior with a closed collar strip protected. Choose C0 errors below the positive distance from 0 and 1 on the compact perturbation support. The perturbation extends by zero. Critical points lie in a compact interior subset and are isolated, hence finite; separate their values by disjoint constant-near-point bumps, bounded in C1 on transition annuli so no new zeros appear. For n=0 assign distinct values to the finite set.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 2.5 and Lemmas 2.6, 2.8, pp.9–18

items.title: Adapted cobordism data extend across the boundary
items.statement: Adapted f extends smoothly to a boundaryless manifold obtained by adding open external collars, with f=t or 1-t there and no added critical points near W. There is a downward field X with df(X)<0 off the interior critical points, the exact local model (2u,-2v), and the prescribed collar directions.
items.proof_plan: Glue open collars in the given coordinates and extend the linear functions. Patch the exact Morse fields with negative coordinate fields away from critical points, protecting smaller Morse charts and collars. Positive weighted sums preserve df(X)<0. Flow is used only until boundary hitting or on compact interior slabs; do not assert completeness on W.
items.source_locator: Lemma 3.2 pp.20–21 and proof of Theorem 3.4 pp.21–23

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Lemma 3.2 pp.20–21 and proof of Theorem 3.4 pp.21–23

items.title: Handle decomposition relative to the incoming boundary
items.statement: A finite relative handle presentation starts with a collar of M0 and adjoins finitely many framed handles D^k x D^{n-k}, 0<=k<=n, with specified attaching embeddings and compatible corner roundings, ending diffeomorphic to W relative to M0. The initial ordering need not be by index.
items.proof_plan: Retain full attaching-region data and boundary identifications; empty M0 starts with the empty manifold.
items.source_locator: Definition of handle decomposition, PDF p.5

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Definition of handle decomposition, PDF p.5

items.title: A framed handle trace admits a compatible morse function
items.statement: The elementary trace of any framed k-handle attachment admits a smooth function with one interior index-k critical point and product germs at its regular incoming and outgoing boundaries. The induced framed attachment is the prescribed one, up to the fixed collar comparison.
items.proof_plan: Use the quadratic q=-|u|^2+|v|^2 on Milnor's trace region |q|<=1, |u|^2|v|^2 bounded. Its non-axis trajectories (e^{-t}u,e^t v) identify the overlap with the product outside the attaching sphere; use q as time. Glue through the supplied framing and check smooth transition maps. At k=0 or n use a ball with a minimum or maximum. Compare to the rounded handle using the earlier local handle-pair result and rounding isotopy.
items.source_locator: Theorem 3.12 complete proof pp.30–31; Lemma 3.7 p.26

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 3.12 complete proof pp.30–31; Lemma 3.7 p.26

items.title: Morse functions and handle decompositions correspond
items.statement: An adapted excellent function yields a relative presentation with one index-k handle for each index-k critical point. Conversely every finite framed relative handle presentation is induced, up to relative diffeomorphism, by an adapted excellent function with that ordered index list.
items.proof_plan: Cut at regular values in the boundaryless extension. Apply one-handle attachment and regular product bands with lower collars fixed. Conversely concatenate the trace functions on disjoint critical-value windows; normalize collar time derivatives before gluing, then positively rescale the global range. Verify finite empty and endpoint cases.
items.source_locator: Corollary 2.10 pp.18–19; Lemma 3.7 p.26; Theorems 3.12–3.13 pp.30–32

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Corollary 2.10 pp.18–19; Lemma 3.7 p.26; Theorems 3.12–3.13 pp.30–32

items.title: Dual handle decomposition
items.statement: The dual presentation is read from M1 in reverse order, interchanging D^k and D^{n-k} in each handle and using the complementary boundary region for attachment.
items.proof_plan: Define through the geometric reversed trace, retaining induced framing; attaching sphere dimension becomes n-k-1 and belt sphere dimension becomes k-1.

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Final upside-down discussion, PDF p.9

items.title: Handle duality from negating a morse function
items.statement: For adapted f on an n-triad the adapted reversed function is 1-f. Its handles have indices n-k in reverse order; cores and cocores, attaching and belt spheres interchange in each elementary trace.
items.proof_plan: In the Morse model 1-f=(1-c)-|v|^2+|u|^2; swap factors and reverse field direction. The outgoing boundary region D^k x S^{n-k-1} becomes the attaching region. For oriented triads reverse W as well. Translation from -f to 1-f changes no differential.

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Final upside-down discussion, PDF p.9

items.title: Critical values of disjoint trajectory closures can be interchanged
items.statement: Let a compact regular slab of adapted (f,X) contain just two critical points, or two finite groups each at one level. Assume their closed trajectory sets within this slab, including boundary endpoints, are disjoint. Prescribe arbitrary new critical levels strictly inside the slab. There is g=f near its boundary, equal to f plus a constant near each critical group, with the same critical points and indices and X still downward gradient-like for g.
items.proof_plan: On the complement of the two critical trajectory sets every orbit crosses the whole slab. Extend a separating boundary cutoff constantly along these orbits, by constants near the compact critical trajectory sets. Prove smoothness there using disjointness, local Morse coordinates, and finite hitting-time continuity. Choose two increasing interval diffeomorphisms fixed near endpoints and translating near the old critical levels; interpolate convexly using the invariant cutoff. Then Xg=(partial G/partial time)Xf<0 and the local Hessians are unchanged. The strictly interior target requirement corrects Nicolaescu's endpoint misprint.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 4.1 and extension 4.2 pp.37–39

items.title: Framed level spheres can be disjoined by a small isotopy
items.statement: If compact embedded P^p,Q^q in a closed d-manifold have p+q<d and P has a supplied product normal neighborhood, an arbitrarily small ambient isotopy supported in that neighborhood moves P off Q.
items.proof_plan: In P x R^{d-p}, Sard applied to the normal projection on Q makes almost every small normal translation disjoint. Realize the translation by a compactly supported normal vector field equal to its constant vector near the path of zero section. Its finite-time flow is the isotopy. Empty spheres need no move.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Lemma 4.6 pp.40–41

items.title: A level isotopy is realized by changing the gradient like field
items.statement: Given a regular compact slab and an isotopy h of one regular level starting at the identity, change the downward field only in the slab interior so its boundary transport is composed with h (with direction stated), retaining f and the local critical-point models.
items.proof_plan: Use ascending normalized field Y=X/df(X), hence Yf=1. In its product coordinates push Y forward by (t,z)->(t,h_t(z)), where h_t is stationary near both ends. Multiply by the original negative function df(X) to obtain a downward field matching X near both ends. Ascending transport becomes h composed with old ascending transport; downward transport is its inverse.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Lemma 4.7 and its construction pp.42–43

items.title: Adjacent inverted index critical levels can be separated dynamically
items.statement: Suppose a compact slab contains only a lower critical group of index k and an upper group of index l<=k. A field perturbation supported near an intermediate regular level removes all trajectories from the upper group to the lower group; their closed critical trajectory sets in the slab are then disjoint.
items.proof_plan: The lower belt spheres have dimension n-k-1, upper attaching spheres l-1; their dimension sum is n+l-k-2<n-1. They are finite disjoint unions with framed neighborhoods. Disjoin them and realize the motion by a field change. Because these are the only two critical levels, any intersection or accumulation connecting the two closed sets would give a connecting orbit; verify this via Morse entry/exit neighborhoods and compact regular-band hitting maps. No global closed-manifold Morse–Smale theorem is invoked.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 4.4 proof pp.40–43

items.title: Morse rearrangement by index
items.statement: On a compact triad, an adapted excellent Morse function can be replaced by an adapted excellent function with the same critical points and indices and with every lower-index point below every higher-index point. The field may be changed; boundary germs stay fixed.
items.proof_plan: Use adjacent inversions in the finite critical index word. Isolate two adjacent levels, apply dynamic separation and interchange, decreasing the inversion number by one without changing other values. Termination gives index order. Repeated starting values may first be separated by the finite bump construction.
items.source_locator: Theorem 4.8 p.44; Nicolaescu proof of Theorem 2.4.11 pp.60–61

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 4.8 p.44; Nicolaescu proof of Theorem 2.4.11 pp.60–61

items.title: Self indexing morse function existence
items.statement: Every compact n-triad has an adapted Morse function with f(p)=(index(p)+1)/(n+2) at all critical points. Starting with any adapted Morse function, retain the critical points and indices while obtaining these values. Such a function need not be excellent.
items.proof_plan: After ordering, successively coalesce adjacent equal-index groups by the group form of rearrangement, first disjoining their level spheres. No trajectories join critical points at equal values. Choose group values with disjoint windows then use a smooth increasing rescaling, fixed in the boundary germs, to attain (k+1)/(n+2). For n=0 all points receive 1/2.
items.source_locator: Theorem 4.8, Definition 4.9 p.44; Nicolaescu Definition 2.4.10 and Theorem 2.4.11 pp.58–61

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 4.8, Definition 4.9 p.44; Nicolaescu Definition 2.4.10 and Theorem 2.4.11 pp.58–61

items.title: Handles of equal index can be attached on one level
items.statement: Every index-k block in a rearranged presentation may be realized as disjoint k-handles attached to one regular lower boundary, with any ordering of those disjoint attachments giving the same relative diffeomorphism type.
items.proof_plan: Use the self-indexing level and simultaneous-attachment theorem on the extended manifold. The disjoint local handles have disjoint transported attaching regions; quotient gluing on disjoint regions commutes. Do not infer independence for arbitrary original attaching maps before the field changes.
items.source_locator: Extension 4.2 and Theorem 4.8 pp.39,44; simultaneous construction pp.35–36

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Extension 4.2 and Theorem 4.8 pp.39,44; simultaneous construction pp.35–36

items.title: Finite cellular approximation for handle models
items.statement: For finite CW complexes K,L and a subcomplex C of K, any map K->L cellular on C is homotopic relative to C to a cellular map.
items.proof_plan: Prove the finite case of cellular approximation: on each source r-cell, remove target cells of dimension >r in decreasing dimension. First use the PL modification in the next proof sentence to miss a point; radially push the punctured target disk to its boundary. For the PL modification, subdivide a cube finely near the preimage of an inner ball in the target open cell, linearly interpolate vertex values in an outer ball, and interpolate with a PL cutoff supported there. Its image near the inner center lies in finitely many r-planes and misses a point when target dimension >r. The half-radius estimate protects the complement. HEP extends each homotopy, fixed on C; only finitely many source and target cells occur.
items.source_locator: Theorem 4.8 with Lemma 4.10 and full proofs pp.349–351

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology — Theorem 4.8 with Lemma 4.10 and full proofs pp.349–351

items.title: Finite cell attachments transport across homotopy equivalences
items.statement: Let u:A->B be a homotopy equivalence and attach finitely many disks to A by alpha. The induced comparison A union_alpha disks -> B union_(u alpha) disks is a homotopy equivalence. The construction is compatible with designated subpairs on which the original inverse and homotopies are supplied.
items.proof_plan: Use a common mapping-cylinder space for u. Attach boundary homotopy cylinders and disk prisms; extend inverse homotopies over each disk by the disk-boundary HEP. Two prism collapses compare the attachments. Explicitly retain the supplied subpair homotopies in the old cylinder, so the conclusion is about pairs and not merely separate total spaces. This is not application of CW HEP to A before A has a CW model.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology — Propositions 0.18–0.19, Corollaries 0.20–0.21 pp.16–17; Exercise 27 p.20

items.title: A handle decomposition gives a relative cw complex
items.statement: A compact smooth triad (W;M0,M1) with a finite relative handle presentation has the homotopy type of a finite CW pair (K,L), with L a finite CW model of M0 and exactly one relative k-cell for each k-handle. The comparison is a homotopy equivalence of pairs, not a claimed literal collapse of all handles simultaneously.
items.proof_plan: First construct a finite CW model for every closed manifold from its finite handles with empty base, using the same following finite induction; that construction does not need a boundary model. This supplies L for M0. After ordering handles, replace each handle by its cell homotopy pair, transport the attaching map to the previous model using the gluing lemma, and cellularly approximate the sphere map. It then lands in the (k-1)-skeleton even if L has higher cells. Attach one k-cell, preserving the comparison of pairs. Arbitrarily ordered presentations are handled by index rearrangement, which preserves all handle counts.
items.source_locator: Milnor Theorem 3.14 pp.32–35, together with Hatcher Theorem 4.8 pp.349–351

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Milnor Theorem 3.14 pp.32–35, together with Hatcher Theorem 4.8 pp.349–351

items.title: A zero handle joined to a boundary collar is absorbed
items.statement: If a new 0-handle is connected to an existing compact n-manifold boundary by a 1-handle with one foot on each component, their union with the old manifold is diffeomorphic to the old manifold relative to its complement away from the attaching patch. Any later attachments can be transported by this diffeomorphism.
items.proof_plan: Give a direct collar proof: the 0-disk with the joining tube is an n-disk attached along a boundary (n-1)-disk. Straighten the specified foot collar and reparametrize the extended collar back into the old collar; interpolate to the identity at its outer boundary and round compatibly. This special endpoint absorption is proved here, without the later general handle-cancellation theorem. For n=1 the construction just shortens a joined interval.
items.source_locator: Disk-attachment lemma on PDF p.8; endpoint corollary p.9

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Disk-attachment lemma on PDF p.8; endpoint corollary p.9

items.title: Connected cobordisms admit presentations without superfluous zero handles
items.statement: A compact connected n-cobordism with nonempty connected incoming boundary admits a relative presentation with no 0-handles.
items.proof_plan: Order handles. Form the finite component graph of the incoming collar and all 0-handles, with 1-handles as edges. Handles of index >=2 cannot join components because their attaching region is connected, so the graph is connected. Grow a tree from the incoming vertex by repeatedly adding an edge to a new vertex; connectivity ensures one exists until all vertices are reached. Attach these tree 1-handles first and absorb each newly joined disk by the local lemma. Transport remaining handles along the resulting diffeomorphisms. n=0 has no such nonempty boundary and the implication is vacuous.

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Endpoint corollary PDF p.9

items.title: Dual elimination of top index handles
items.statement: A compact connected n-cobordism with nonempty connected outgoing boundary admits a presentation relative to its incoming boundary with no n-handles.
items.proof_plan: Apply zero-handle elimination to the reversed triad and dualize. This is a separate existence statement; no unproved simultaneous preservation of an already normalized opposite end is asserted.

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Endpoint corollary PDF p.9

items.title: Product cobordisms have critical point free presentations
items.statement: For a closed smooth M the product M x [0,1] has the critical-point-free adapted projection and an empty relative handle presentation. Conversely an adapted function without critical points gives a product triad, fixing the incoming end.
items.proof_plan: Projection has nonzero differential on the interval direction. Conversely use normalized finite-time flow on the compact collar-extended band and its unique inverse. Empty M gives empty W. No assertion is made about a preassigned outgoing parametrization.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Definition 3.3 and Theorem 3.4 pp.21–23

items.title: Handle decompositions are not canonical
items.statement: A relative diffeomorphism type can have different Morse functions, fields, critical values, and framed attaching data. Rearrangement changes the presentation. Self-indexing need not be excellent. No full Cerf theorem or uniqueness of a minimal handle count is claimed.
items.proof_plan: Explain choices and distinguish existence from uniqueness; the later elementary-moves page owns general cancellation and slides.
items.source_locator: Theorem 4.8 p.44 and opening of Section 5 p.45

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 4.8 p.44 and opening of Section 5 p.45

title: Handle Decompositions Duality and Rearrangement — Examples

items.title: Relative handle decomposition of a cylinder
items.statement: For S^1 x [0,1], f(z,t)=t has no critical points and the relative handle list is empty. Reversal uses 1-t and also has an empty list.
items.proof_plan: Compute df(partial_t)=1 and exhibit identity product coordinates; both boundary circles are retained.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 3.4 pp.21–23

items.title: Dual handle presentations of a genus g surface
items.statement: The orientable closed genus-g surface made from one disk, 2g orientation-compatible bands in the standard paired arrangement, and one cap has handle counts (1,2g,1); its reversed presentation has the same counts, with the original disk and cap exchanged.
items.proof_plan: Specify the standard 4g-gon paired-edge boundary word and thicken its one-vertex graph; verify the resulting band boundary is a single circle before adding the cap. At g=0 this is two disks along their boundary. Do not cite a B-homed surface example as a dependency.
items.source_locator: Surface handle illustration PDF pp.5–6 and reversal p.9

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Surface handle illustration PDF pp.5–6 and reversal p.9

items.title: Reordering independent one handles
items.statement: On a disk choose four disjoint boundary arcs and attach two oriented 1-handles using two paired arcs. They can be attached in either order or simultaneously, with the same framed attaching data and resulting surface.
items.proof_plan: Both quotients identify disjoint regions of the same disjoint union, so they agree. Choose the two trace functions to put their critical points at either order or the same value; no connecting trajectory is imposed between the independent handles.

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Disjoint attachment ordering, PDF pp.7–8

items.title: Critical levels cannot always be interchanged across a connecting trajectory
items.statement: For f(x,y,z)=(z+1)/2 on S^2 there is an explicitly rescaled round negative gradient X, downward gradient-like in the exact local Morse convention, with a trajectory from the maximum p to minimum q. Every function g for which this fixed X is downward gradient-like satisfies g(p)>g(q); their values cannot be reversed while retaining X.
items.proof_plan: Let X0=-grad_round f. Near north use Morse polar radius r=sqrt((1-z)/2), so X0 has radial coefficient (1+z)r/4; near south use r=sqrt((1+z)/2), with coefficient -(1-z)r/4. Choose a smooth positive multiplier a(z) equal to 8/(1+z) near north and 8/(1-z) near south, interpolated to 1 away from the poles. Then X=aX0 is exactly 2u at the maximum and -2v at the minimum in Cartesian Morse coordinates. Its meridian trajectories have the same images as those of X0, whose height is z(t)=-tanh(t/2); positive bounded rescaling preserves the two infinite-time limits. For Xg<0 and finite s<t, g(p)>=g(gamma(s))>g(gamma(t))>=g(q). The class is nonempty since g=f qualifies.

references.title: Milnor, Lectures on the h-Cobordism Theorem — Theorem 4.1 hypothesis pp.37–39; explicit sphere witness is an adaptation

items.title: Empty incoming boundary requires zero handles
items.statement: A nonempty closed connected n-manifold presented from the empty incoming boundary must use a 0-handle; S^n has one 0-handle and one n-handle for n>=1. The endpoint-elimination theorem therefore needs its boundary hypothesis.
items.proof_plan: Before any 0-handle, a positive-index handle has nonempty attaching region and cannot attach to the empty set. Construct S^n by gluing two n-disks along their full boundary. For n=0 each point itself is a 0-handle.

references.title: Etnyre, PCMI 2019, Handlebody Decompositions — Endpoint discussion PDF pp.1,9

items.title: Self indexing values on a two dimensional cobordism
items.statement: In dimension two the normalized index levels are 1/4,1/2,3/4. Two index-one points share value 1/2, so self-indexing does not imply excellent.
items.proof_plan: Compute (k+1)/4 for k=0,1,2 and use the two independent bands to realize repeated index-one critical values. Small disjoint bumps give excellence at the expense of exact self-indexing.

references.title: Nicolaescu, An Invitation to Morse Theory, second edition — Definition 2.4.10 and Theorem 2.4.11 pp.58–61
